audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage (Wonderly 1951 sec. 1.6) is verbatim in the held IJAL 17(2) scanned under the p.108 running header, including the trisyllabic example [,min'ge?tu] that justifies the catalog's 110 (secondary on syllable 1 + primary penult) against StressTyp2's 010; the catalog's contra note is correct. The record's top-level quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty even though sources[0] and the domain quotation/the domain locator carry the full citation and text — fill them (grade should reflect: primary source held, page-verified). (2) Deciding source: a 1951 structuralist phonology article that is part of the only full description of Copainalá Zoque (Wonderly's IJAL series = dissertation); first-hand fieldwork; the author hedges ('general but incomplete') and states the rule over the stress group, which the record already flags as domain word and phrase together. Glottolog lists no later phonology of this languoid. (3)

sources.quote: '(1) Si una palabra está formada de dos sílabas, el acento cae en la primera sílaba. (2) Si una palabra está formada de más de dos sílabas, el acento principal cae en la penúltima sílaba. ... minu ... mi; mingue'tu ... gue'; mingue'tutij ... tu. En este diccionario hay algunas otras palabras que no siguen las reglas anteriores, y llevan acento escrito (tuchtucujú' "torcaza"; siquití'n "chicharra").' sources.quote: Quotes Wonderly: '"A stress group may be said to consist of a single word... or a close-knit phrase ...
